drills.q: 50M-doc RAG system on GCP: name every layer and one decision per layer.
drills.a: Chunk+embed (batch mode ~50% off ~) -> Vector Search (billion-scale headroom, filtered namespaces) -> Gemini Flash serving with cached static prefix -> citation-forced prompts + eval CI -> dedicated agent identities. Layer decisions: corpus size justifies managed ANN; Flash for volume, Pro routed for hard queries.

drills.q: 'Why not just paste the whole wiki into the 1M window instead of RAG?' Answer with economics.
drills.a: 400k-token corpus re-sent per query = linear cost unless cached; caches bill TTL storage and expire; latency 30-90s first token at that span (~); citations unreliable. RAG: embed once, ~2-4k tokens/query. Long context wins one-shot analysis of static docs, not repeated queries.

drills.q: Team of two needs a stateful multi-tool agent live in weeks. ADK where, and why?
drills.a: ADK on Agent Engine: sessions/Memory Bank/auth wired by the platform while they build logic. Two devs rebuilding session stores on Cloud Run burn runway. Revisit portability when platform team exists.

drills.q: Filtered Vector Search returns fewer than k neighbors. Bug or feature?
drills.a: Feature: pre-filtering restricts candidates before ANN traversal, so sparse filters legitimately yield short result sets - post-filtering would pad with irrelevant hits. Confirm which behavior your client expects and design k accordingly.

drills.q: Agent bill tripled month-over-month. Diagnose in order.
drills.a: 1) usage_metadata per feature: history growth into prompts? thinking tokens globally on? 2) -latest alias moved traffic to pricier version? 3) cache TTL misaligned (all misses)? 4) retry storms multiplying calls? Fix: compact histories, cap thinking budgets, pin versions, restructure prefixes, per-feature unit dashboards.

drills.q: Design evaluation for an agent before allowing prompt changes to ship.
drills.a: Golden sets (input->expected outcome/tool trajectory) in CI; LLM-as-judge rubrics calibrated against human-labeled subsets; refusal-behavior tests alongside accuracy; shadow new model versions against live traffic before alias switches. Judge disagreement is fine as regression detection, not ground truth.

drills.q: When do you self-host vLLM on GKE instead of calling Gemini API? Give the break-even intuition.
drills.a: Residency bars, custom/open weights, steady high volume amortizing GPU pools, deep serving control. Sustained utilization above roughly half of GPU capacity favors owning; below it API zero-idle wins. Include ops labor - teams underestimate 24/7 GPU fleets.

drills.q: RAG agent cites sources but users report wrong answers. What's broken?
drills.a: Citation presence != fidelity. Add claim-level entailment checks against retrieved chunks, sample-audit judge agreement, log low-confidence paths for human review, gate generation on retrieval-similarity thresholds. Perfect prevention impossible; measured degradation detection is the goal.

drills.q: Prompt injection succeeds against your agent. Why does identity design decide the blast radius?
drills.a: If the agent runs as a broad human/shared credential, injection inherits those permissions. Dedicated agent identity + least-privilege tool roles + app-level authz inside tools confines it to the agent's own narrow scope regardless of injected instructions.

drills.q: 2M-vector internal search over HR docs - Vector Search or AlloyDB AI? Defend.
drills.a: AlloyDB AI (ScaNN indexes, pgvector-compatible): below the ~10M threshold where managed ANN pays; same database serves operational data, less infra, simpler ops. Vector Search earns its cost at billion-scale/high-QPS - headroom nobody uses here is platform tax.
